commentary_title: Resilient Asian import demand and Atlantic exports support VLCC activity
commentary_summary: VLCC utilisation stood at 89.6% indicating stronger vessel employment as more ships moved from waiting positions into active trading. Underlying demand remained supported by long-haul crude movements from the Atlantic Basin to Asia. Tonne-mile index remained above the annual baseline at 103.3 and was 7.3% higher than a year ago, indicating that voyage distances continue to support vessel demand. | Asian demand remained relatively resilient. Chinese discharge activity stabilised after recent weakness, while India continued to demonstrate steady crude import requirements. The Pacific region maintained healthy levels of laden vessel activity, reinforcing Asia's role as the primary demand centre for VLCCs. | Continued crude exports from the US Gulf, Brazil and West Africa, combined with stable Asian import requirements, helped maintain a favourable demand environment for VLCCs.
